t.4.47.2: Having gone a long way together with all those excellent monkeys, he searched the caves and the thickets of the Vindhya.
t.4.47.1: The monkey Hanumān, having set out together with Tāra and Aṅgada, began to explore that region just as Sugrīva had directed.
t.4.47.4: Searching the region on every side, all those heroic vānaras did not find Sītā, the princess of Mithilā, the daughter of Janaka.
t.4.47.3: From the mountain summit they searched the places made impassable by rivers, the lakes, the great trees, the various clusters of trees, and the mountains dense with trees.
t.4.47.5: Eating roots and fruits of many kinds, those unassailable ones, searching, dwelt here and there. But that vast region, full of caves and dense thickets, was hard to search.
t.4.47.6: Then, leaving that region behind, all the leaders of the monkey troops, fearing nothing from any quarter, entered another region that was hard to approach.
t.4.47.7: Where the trees bear barren fruit, flowerless and stripped of leaves, where the rivers are without water, and where even roots are very hard to find.
t.4.47.8: Where there are no buffaloes, no deer, and no elephants, nor tigers, nor birds, nor any other creatures that roam the forest.
t.4.47.9: Where, on dry land, there are lotus plants with glossy leaves and fully blossomed lotuses, lovely to behold and fragrant, yet shunned even by the bees.
t.4.47.10: There was a great sage named Kaṇḍu, highly fortunate, truthful in speech and rich in austerities, extremely wrathful and, by virtue of his religious observances, difficult to assail.
t.4.47.12: By that righteous-souled one the whole of that great forest there was cursed, so that it became shelterless, hard to approach, and devoid of beasts and birds.
t.4.47.11: In that forest his son, a boy of ten years, perished, meeting the end of his life; and there the great sage became enraged.
t.4.47.14: Even there, those great-souled ones, eager to do what was pleasing to Sugrīva, did not see the daughter of Janaka, nor Rāvaṇa, her abductor.
t.4.47.13: Then, with minds intent, they searched its forest borders, the caves of the mountains, and the sources of the rivers.
t.4.47.15: Having entered that dreadful place, overgrown with creepers and thickets, they saw an asura of cruel deeds who had no fear of the gods.
t.4.47.16: Seeing him, terrible, standing there like another mountain, all the monkeys, beholding him who resembled a mountain, girded themselves tightly.
t.4.47.17: He too, the mighty one, said to all those monkeys, “You are done for!” and, enraged, rushed at them with his clenched fist raised.
t.4.47.18: Then Aṅgada, the son of Vālin, as that one came suddenly rushing at him,
t.4.47.20: The asura fell to the ground like an overturned mountain. When he lay breathless there, the victorious vānaras searched that entire mountain cave almost everywhere.
t.4.47.21: Then, having searched the forest thoroughly, they all once again entered yet another dreadful mountain cavern.
t.4.47.19: Thinking, “This is Rāvaṇa,” he struck him with the palm of his hand. Struck by the son of Vālin, he vomited blood from his mouth.
t.4.47.22: Having pondered again, weary, they came forth and gathered together; and in a secluded place, at the foot of a tree, they sat down, dejected in mind.
